question: What is the main goal of family planning?

options.A: Permanently stopping population growth in rural areas
options.B: Deciding the number and spacing of children
options.C: Ensuring every woman gives birth in a hospital
options.D: Treating all known sexually transmitted infections

explanation: Spot on! Family planning simply helps couples and individuals choose how many kids they want and the best time to have them. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T53#GNS214_U1_T53_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT part of routine family planning services?
explanation: You got it! Family planning clinics focus on counseling, birth control, and fertility support—not major operations like removing an appendix. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T53#GNS214_U1_T53_h1)

question: What is the minimum recommended interval between pregnancies to protect maternal and child health?
explanation: Spacing pregnancies by at least two years gives the mother's body enough time to recover and lowers infant health risks. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T53#GNS214_U1_T53_h2)

question: A nursing mother visits the clinic 6 months after delivery. Why is birth spacing important for her next pregnancy?

options.A: It prevents the infant from developing childhood illnesses
options.B: It allows her body and nutrient stores to fully recover
options.C: It guarantees that the next child will have no health issues
options.D: It eliminates the need for antenatal care later

explanation: Exactly! Giving the body a break restores vital nutrients like iron so the mother is strong and ready for the next pregnancy. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T53#GNS214_U1_T53_h2)

question: Which of the following is classified as a barrier method of contraception?
explanation: Condoms act as physical barriers that prevent sperm from entering the female reproductive tract. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T53#GNS214_U1_T53_h3)

question: How do combined hormonal contraceptive pills mainly prevent pregnancy?

options.A: By creating a permanent blockage in the fallopian tubes
options.B: By destroying sperm cells on contact
options.C: By causing early shedding of the womb lining every week
options.D: By stopping ovulation and thickening cervical mucus

explanation: Well done! These hormones trick the body into not releasing an egg while also making it hard for sperm to swim through. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T53#GNS214_U1_T53_h3)

question: What is your main role as a nurse during family planning counseling?

options.B: To convince every young person to get sterilized
options.C: To provide clear information so the client can choose freely
options.D: To choose the best contraceptive method for the client

explanation: Correct! As nurses, we guide and educate without forcing our personal choices on our patients. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T53#GNS214_U1_T53_h4)

question: A client wants a specific pill, but it is unsafe for her because she has severe high blood pressure. What should you do first?

options.A: Give her the requested pill anyway to make her happy
options.B: Send her straight to a big teaching hospital for surgery
options.C: Scold her for choosing a bad medication without asking
options.D: Explain the health risk gently and discuss safer options

explanation: You got it! Patient safety comes first. We calmly explain why a drug isn't safe and gladly help them pick a better alternative. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T53#GNS214_U1_T53_h4)

question: What infection prevention practice is most important when inserting a contraceptive implant under the skin?

options.C: Making the patient fast for 12 hours

explanation: Spot on! Even though it's a minor procedure, keeping everything strictly sterile protects your patient from nasty wound infections. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T53#GNS214_U1_T53_h5)

question: Why is keeping a proper inventory of family planning supplies so important at a clinic?

options.A: It ensures expired drugs get handed out very fast
options.B: It means you don't have to write daily attendance records
options.C: It lets the nurse sell extra supplies for side cash
options.D: It stops stock-outs so clients don't suddenly run out of their method

explanation: Great thinking! Running out of supplies leaves patients stranded and unprotected, so tracking inventory keeps care running smoothly. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T53#GNS214_U1_T53_h5)

question: Which side effect is very common with progestin-only injectable contraceptives (like Depo-Provera)?

options.C: Sudden swelling of the thyroid gland

explanation: Correct! Injectables often change how periods look—some spotting, heavier days, or periods stopping completely are quite normal. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T53#GNS214_U1_T53_h6)

question: A client comes back complaining of mild spotting a month after getting an implant. How should you respond?

options.A: Tell her she has a serious pelvic infection
options.B: Take out the implant immediately and offer nothing else
options.C: Reassure her that this is a normal and common side effect
options.D: Tell her to stop drinking water for two days

explanation: Spot on! Pre-counseling helps clients stay calm. Reassuring them that spotting is normal builds great trust and keeps them comfortable. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T53#GNS214_U1_T53_h6)

question: What is a common myth that stops people from using family planning in many communities?

options.A: Family planning guarantees you will have a baby boy
options.B: Contraceptives are made only by local farmers
options.C: Using a condom cures all infections instantly

explanation: You nailed it! A lot of people fear that using birth control now means they won't be able to bear children later, which isn't true. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T53#GNS214_U1_T53_h7)

question: You notice women in a village want birth control but are scared of their husbands' reactions. What should be your main step?

options.A: Give out contraceptives in secret without telling anyone
options.B: Report all the husbands to the nearest police station
options.C: Organize community talks to involve men in reproductive health education
options.D: Close the clinic until the village changes its culture

explanation: Brilliant approach! Bringing men into the conversation clears up myths, reduces home conflicts, and builds teamwork for family health. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T53#GNS214_U1_T53_h7)
